Order on Civil Misc. Delay Condonation and Substitution Application Nos. 49803 and 49804 of
2004
1.
Learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for the respondents are present.

2.  This delay condonation application has been filed for condoning the delay in moving the substitution application to bring on record the LRs of deceased-appellant no.3, Kartar Singh, who has died on 11.09.1992, leaving behind his two sons, namely Darshan Singh and Dalbeer Singh.
It is further submitted that Darshan Singh has also died on 07.09.2001, leaving behind his widow Kulveendar Kaur and two sons, namely Sandeep Singh and Mandeep Singh.
Order on Civil Misc. Delay Condonation and Substitution Application Nos. 49805 and 49806 of 2004 1.
Learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for the respondents are present.

2. This delay condonation application has been filed for condoning the delay in moving the substitution application to bring on record the LRs of deceased-appellant, Dalbeer Singh, who has died on 22.09.1997, leaving behind his minor grand son Charanjeet Singh as his sole heir.

3. Leaned counsel for the appellants submitted that the above substitution applications could not be filed within time because the legal heirs were not aware that they are to be substituted on record being the legal heirs of the deceased-appellants.
4. An affidavit has been filed in support of the delay condonation applications, which is uncontroverted.
The cause shown for filing the above substitution applications with delay, is sufficient.
5. Accordingly, the delay in filing the substitution applications is condoned.
6. All the above mentioned delay condonation and substitution applications are allowed.
7. Learned counsel for the appellants is directed to amend the memo of appeal, accordingly.
Order on Appeal 1.
Heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned Standing Counsel.

2. The instant first appeal under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been filed by the land owners against the award and decree dated 07.12.1988 passed by Sri B.K. Srivastava, District Judge, Rampur in L.A.R. No.23 of 1987, Bhag Singh & others vs. L.A.O. & another, whereby for the Bhag Singh And Others vs Land Acquisition Officer And Another on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196372601/
2 land acquired in village Bharatpur, Tehsil Bilsapur, District Rampur, compensation at the rate of Rs.17,000/- per acre, alongwith other statutory benefits admissible under the Land Acquisition Act,
1894, has been awarded to the land owners.

First Appeal No.1245 of 1990, Ram Charan Dass Vs. L.A.O. & another vide order dated 20.04.2022 and First Appeal No.154 of 1990, Prithipal Singh & others Vs. State of U.P. vide order dated 08.07.2022, has awarded enhanced compensation at the rate of Rs.50,000/- per acre, which has attained finality, because the State has not challenged the above orders before the Apex Court.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the appellants land was acquired for constructing broad gauge railway line between Rampur-Haldwani vide notification under Section 4(1) dated 14.11.1981, which is similar to the acquired land regarding which, this Court has awarded compensation at the rate of Rs.50,000/- per acre, as such, the appellants are also entitled to get enhanced compensation at the same rate, alongwith other statutory benefits provided under the Land Acquisition Act.
5. Per contra, learned Standing Counsel has admitted that the order passed by this Court in the above mentioned appeals, has not been challenged by the State before the Apex Court.

6. Learned Standing Counsel further submitted that the appellants may not be awarded interest on the enhanced amount of compensation awarded by this Court for the period during which, the deficiency of court fees was not made good.

7. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, it is apparent that the appellants land situated in village Bharatpur, Tehsil Bilaspur, District Rampur was acquired for constructing the broad gauge railway line between Rampur-Haldwani vide notification under Section 4(1) of the Act dated 14.11.1981.
Subsequently the Collector made award regarding the acquired land on 22.09.1986 at the rate of Rs.12,000/- per acre.
The possession of the land was taken on 19.09.1986.

The land owners preferred reference, which was allowed vide impugned award and decree dated 07.12.1988 whereby the compensation was enhanced from Rs.12,000/- per acre to Rs.17,000/- per acre besides, other statutory benefits admissible under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
8.

It is also apparent that land of many villages were acquired for constructing the above railway line, and for the land situated in village Debdiba, Rampur, this Court in First Appeal No.154 of 1990,
Prithipal Singh & others Vs. State of U.P., vide order dated 08.07.2022; for the land situated in village Inderpur, Tehsil Bilaspur, District Rampur, in First Appeal No.153 of 1990, Daljeet Singh &
others Vs. State of U.P., vide order dated 20.04.2022; and for the land situated in village Bharatpur,
in First Appeal No.1245 of 1990, Ram Charan Dass Vs. L.A.O. & another, vide order dated 20.04.2022; has already awarded enhanced compensation for the land acquired through notification dated 14.11.1981 at the rate of Rs.50,000/- per acre, which has not been challenged by the State before the Apex Court and as such, the matter has attained finality.

sentences.text:
In view of these facts, the appellants are also entitled to get compensation for their acquired land at the same rate, as has been determined by this Court in all the above mentioned appeals, because the appellants land is similarly situated and was acquired through the same notification dated 14.11.1981.
10.
Accordingly, this appeal is allowed.

The appellants are entitled to get enhanced compensation at the rate of Rs. 50,000/- per acre along with 30% solatium, additional compensation @ 12% per annum and interest under Section 28, as provided under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
11.
This appeal was filed on 08.03.1989, but the deficiency of the court fees was made good on 26.08.1992

, as such, the appellants are not entitled to get any statutory interest on the enhanced compensation for the above mentioned period between 08.03.1989 to 26.08.1992.
12.
However, in the facts and circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs.
13. Office is directed to prepare the decree accordingly.
